chunks: 127 - A group of the Jews came to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, and asked him about matters. Among what they asked him was: “Inform us, O Muhammad, for what reason are these four limbs washed in wudu (ablution), while they are the cleanest parts of the body?”

The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said: “When Shaytan whispered to Adam, peace be upon him, he drew near to the tree and looked at it, so the water of his face departed. Then he stood and walked toward it, and that was the first foot that walked toward the sin. Then he took with his hand from it what was upon it and ate, so the ornaments and garments flew away from his body. Then Adam placed his hand upon the crown of his head and wept.”

So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, accepted his repentance, Allah made obligatory upon him and upon his descendants the purification of these four limbs. Thus Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the washing of the face because he had looked at the tree; He commanded him to wash the two hands up to the elbows because he had taken with them; He commanded him to wipe the head because he had placed his hand upon the crown of his head; and He commanded him to wipe the two feet because he had walked with them toward the sin.”

key_terms.الشَّجَرَةِ: the tree connected to Adam’s trial
key_terms.الْجَوَارِحُ الْأَرْبَعُ: the four limbs purified in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْخَطِيئَةِ: the sin or act of disobedience

ai.seo_question: Why are the face, hands, head, and feet specifically purified in wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the reason for washing and wiping the four limbs in wudu (ablution) by linking them to the actions of Adam عليه السلام when he approached the tree. It presents wudu (ablution) as a divinely mandated purification for Adam عليه السلام and his descendants, connecting ritual purity to repentance and human conduct.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.127 - A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (sw) and asked Him about various matters. Among the questions they asked was:
‘Tell us, O’ Muhammad, why these four parts are washed in ablution when they are the cleanest parts of the body?'

The Prophet (sw) replied: "When Satan whispered to Adam (as), he approached the tree and looked at it, and thus he lost the brightness of his face. Then he walked towards it—this was the first step taken towards wrongdoing.
He reached out with his hand to take from it, and he ate. Consequently, the ornaments and coverings left his body, and he placed his hands on his head and wept.

When Allah (swt), Mighty and Majestic, accepted his repentance, He made it obligatory upon him and his descendants to purify these four parts.
Thus, Allah (swt) commanded the washing of the face because he had looked at the tree, the washing of the hands up to the elbows because he had used them to take from it, the wiping of the head because he had placed his hand on his head, and the wiping of the feet because he had walked with them towards the wrongdoing (khatee'ah)."
